solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Firm is business without any piece of legislation

indicators.note: without tells us to drop the word any from the business word, leaving its first four letters

parts.note: a company is a business
taken as written, the letters removed
an act is a piece of legislation passed by parliament

explanation.surface: A company appears to be operating free of any regulation at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' reads as a noun, a business, but defines the adjective; 'without' here means minus.
explanation.definitionFit: Something compact is solid and dense, which is one sense of firm as an adjective.

clue.text: Mostly get on well with the fellow offering banality

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the next word is used

parts.note: to click with someone is to get on well
he refers to the fellow

explanation.surface: Getting along nicely with a man who only offers platitudes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts CLICK to CLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliché is a trite, overused remark, a piece of banality.

clue.text: Number turning up in protest — who don't republicans want?

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the protest word

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the number abbreviation is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A number is turning up at an anti-monarchy demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' means read from the bottom, so reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Republicans oppose rule by a king or queen, so a sovereign ruler is what they reject.

clue.text: Pole leaving Egypt on a journey to safety

definitions.text: Pole leaving Egypt on a journey to safety

parts.words: Pole leaving Egypt on a journey to safety
parts.note: the staff carried by Moses' brother as the Israelites fled Egypt in the Exodus

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a person from Poland, but it is a staff. In Exodus, Aaron's staff worked wonders before the Israelites escaped Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron's rod is the biblical staff of Moses' brother, carried during the flight from Egypt.

clue.text: Processed mincemeat I had originally: that takes us back!

indicators.note: processed suggests food put through a mincer, so these letters are reworked
originally picks the first letter of the word had

explanation.surface: Mincemeat I'd eaten as a child brings back memories, a Proustian moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives H from had; 'Processed' shuffles MINCEMEAT, I and H.
explanation.definitionFit: A time machine is a fictional device for travelling to the past, carrying people back.

clue.text: Move awkwardly as lass gaining speed outside university

indicators.note: outside says the lass-plus-speed pair wraps around the university letter
gaining means the lass acquires the speed after her

parts.note: a gal is a girl or lass
MPH, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: A girl hurrying off campus moves clumsily as she picks up pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts GALMPH round U.
explanation.definitionFit: To galumph is to move in a heavy, clumsy, lumbering way, a word coined by Lewis Carroll.

clue.text: Talk and pant, no end

indicators.note: no end means the final letter of the panting word is dropped

parts.note: to gasp is to pant

explanation.surface: Someone chatters and gasps endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' cuts GASP to its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas is informal for idle chatter or talk, both noun and verb.

clue.text: Article about friend — all in French — becoming monster

indicators.note: about means the article goes round the friend word

parts.note: la is a French definite article, the
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a friend, written in French, turns into a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all in French' is the signal that both the article and the friend are French words, not English ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamia is a mythical female monster, a serpent-woman who devoured children.

clue.text: My old suspicion is voiced — pay attention!

indicators.note: is voiced means the phrase is spoken aloud, giving the sound of the answer

parts.note: mine is an old form of my (mine eyes), and doubt is suspicion, giving mine doubt

explanation.surface: Someone voices an old suspicion and warns others to listen.
explanation.walkthrough: MINE is archaic for MY before a vowel; 'mine doubt' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mind out is a warning to take care, an imperative to be careful and watch out.

clue.text: Potential grub for horse — eats food round end of day

indicators.note: round means the eating and food pieces go around the picked letter

parts.note: to have a meal is to eat, so has means eats

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word day

parts.note: tack is slang for food, as in hard tack

explanation.surface: A horse eats its food at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: TACK is old slang for food, as in hardtack, the ship's biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A haystack is a pile of stored hay, which a horse could eat.

clue.text: Yours truly's taking in good female American who needs education

indicators.note: taking in means the setter's self-reference holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: yours truly is the setter, so yours truly's means I am, contracted to IM
Nora is a female name

explanation.surface: The setter seems to be hosting a nice American woman in need of schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts G and NORA between the I and M of I'M. The definition stands for 'one who needs education'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant, uninformed person, someone badly in want of learning.

clue.text: Devil bumping off king in capital?

indicators.note: bumping off means killing, so the king letter is removed from the devil word

parts.note: a monkey is a mischievous child, a little devil
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A devil seems to be assassinating a monarch in some capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumping off' removes K from MONKEY. 'capital' reads as a city but is wealth, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is accumulated wealth or funds, which is money.

clue.text: One bird or another crossing river with duck

indicators.note: crossing means the other bird stretches across, enclosing, the next two pieces

parts.note: another bird here is a hen

indicators.note: with joins the river letter to the duck letter

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: One bird or another is seen flying over a river with a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts RO inside HEN. 'duck' is cricket's zero, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a long-legged wading bird, so it is one example of a bird.

clue.text: Potter having a stint on Scottish island

indicators.note: on means placed after, the stint coming on top of the island

parts.note: Muck is a small island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland
a bout is a spell or stint of activity

explanation.surface: A potter, perhaps Harry, spending some time on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a name or a craftsman but is the verb, to idle about.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to pass time aimlessly, and muck about is the idiom for that.

clue.text: Happiness interrupted by supervisor that's cut short loud game

indicators.note: interrupted by means the happiness word is broken into by the next pieces

parts.note: cheer is gladness or happiness

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter of the supervisor word is dropped

parts.note: a minder is someone who looks after or supervises
f, forte, is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A noisy game cuts short the good cheer of a supervisor.
explanation.walkthrough: A minder is a bodyguard or carer; F (forte) is the musical mark for loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemin de fer is a card game related to baccarat, popular in casinos.

clue.text: Feature provided by architect is arc strangely positioned

indicators.note: strangely positioned says the letters of the three preceding words are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A building's notable feature, an arc the architect has placed oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic is a distinguishing trait or quality, a feature of something.

clue.text: Composer's third and fifth maybe

parts.note: a third and a fifth are musical distances between notes, which a composer uses

explanation.walkthrough: 'third and fifth' look like symphony numbers or movements, but they are gaps between notes.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, a third and a fifth are pitch spacings between two notes, examples of the musical term.

clue.text: Male in truth that is the type to exude charm

indicators.note: in places the male letter inside the truth word

parts.note: sooth is an archaic word for truth, as in forsooth
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A truthful man, that is, the charming type.
explanation.walkthrough: Sooth survives today mainly in 'soothsayer' and 'forsooth'.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoothie is a suave, ingratiating person who uses charm to get their way.

clue.text: Mismanages boy, tiny, limited by teachers

indicators.note: limited by means hemmed in by, so the teachers enclose the boy and tiny pieces

parts.note: masters are schoolteachers
a lad is a boy
mini means very small, tiny

explanation.surface: A small boy is supposedly mishandled while hemmed in by his schoolmasters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited by' puts LADMINI inside MASTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To maladminister is to run or administer badly, the same as to mismanage.

clue.text: Rhetorical device in stories enthralling small child

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the stories word holds the child word inside

parts.note: stories, in the sense of fibs, are lies
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: Bedtime stories captivating a young child use a figure of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stories' are fibs here, not tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is ironic understatement by negating the opposite, as in not bad, a figure of speech.

clue.text: Hunt maybe led by artist and explorer

indicators.note: led by means the artist letters come first, ahead of the hunt word

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
Leigh Hunt was an English poet and essayist, so Hunt is an example of a Leigh

explanation.surface: A hunting party is led by an artist and an explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunt' looks like a chase but is the writer Leigh Hunt. Sir Walter Raleigh was an Elizabethan explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was an English adventurer who led voyages to the Americas.

clue.text: Warm hospital with encouragement to enjoy food

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
eat up is what one says to urge someone to finish their meal

explanation.surface: A hospital warms patients and urges them to finish their food.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat up is to make warmer, to warm something.

clue.text: Those people joining cricket side stop improving

indicators.note: joining means the next piece is attached after the cricket side

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
them means those people
to end is to stop

explanation.surface: People joining a cricket team stop getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: The ON side is the half of a cricket field on the batsman's legs side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the mend is recovering, getting better after illness or injury.

clue.text: Woman's number, having changed sides

definitions.note: the def is woman with 's standing for is, so the woman is the answer

indicators.note: changing sides swaps right for left, so the R letter becomes L

parts.note: a number here is something that numbs, and ether is an anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A woman's telephone number has changed after she switched teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as numb-er, an anaesthetic; 'having changed sides' turns its R (right) into L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel is a woman's given name, so it names one woman.

clue.text: Lunar feature of note, not well covered

indicators.note: covered means the note sits around, covering, the unwell word

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
ill means not well

explanation.surface: Something on the moon is notable, and someone unwell is wrapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of note' looks like 'notable', but note is the sol-fa syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: A rille is a long narrow channel or groove on the Moon's surface.

clue.text: Covering needed by thatcher

indicators.note: needed by suggests the letters are found within the next word, which contains them

explanation.surface: A roof thatcher needs some sort of covering for his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed by' says the answer sits inside 'thatcher'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatch is a door or cover over an opening, as on a ship's deck.

clue.text: Clever — when full of worry is inclined to give up

indicators.note: when full of means the clever word holds the next two pieces inside it

parts.note: deft means skilful or clever
to eat someone is to worry or trouble them, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A clever person, once worried, is prone to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: Worry as eat is the 'what's eating you?' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A defeatist attitude expects failure and readily surrenders, so it is prone to quitting.

clue.text: Person wanting payment cheated, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word for cheated is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: to be done is to be cheated or swindled

explanation.surface: Someone owed money says they were swindled.
explanation.definitionFit: A dun is a creditor or debt collector who demands repayment.

clue.text: One Greek character or another abandoning university after end of course

indicators.note: after means the trimmed Greek letter follows the picked letter
end of picks the final letter of the word course
abandoning means the university letter is dropped from the other Greek character

parts.note: another Greek character here is upsilon

explanation.surface: A Greek student leaves university at the end of the course.
explanation.walkthrough: Both answer and the 'another' character are Greek letters; the second loses its opening U.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Fruit became more fashionable

parts.note: rose means increased, became more
hip means trendy or fashionable

explanation.surface: Some fruit grew more in vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosehip is the red seed-pod fruit of the rose plant.
